Attributes, aliases and conversion

Source: vignettes/attributes.Rmd
attributes.Rmd

What problem does this solve?

Energy models, statistics and inventories carve fuels into categories, and every source carves differently: an inventory guideline lists fifty-odd fuels, a model has a handful of commodity codes, a chart wants a dozen colours. The numbers that turn one quantity into another – a net calorific value in GJ/t, a CO2 factor in kg/TJ – are published per category, for some categories, and the category a figure is published for is rarely the one the data is keyed by.

A nested scale keeps such numbers as attributes: values that belong to a member at whatever level they are published, resolved down the hierarchy when a finer member has none of its own, and applied row by row. The same mechanism serves any dimension – an area per region, an hour count per time slice – but fuels are where it earns its keep, so this vignette works on a small fuel taxonomy.

An example taxonomy

Eight fuels under five carriers under three groups. The values attached to them are round numbers chosen for illustration, not reference data: a net calorific value (lhv, GJ/t) for five fuels and a CO2 factor (ef_co2, kg/TJ) for four, under the source "example".

values <- data.frame(
  frame = "fuel",
  member = c("Anthracite", "Bituminous", "Lignite", "NaturalGas", "Biodiesel",
           "Anthracite", "Lignite", "NaturalGas", "Biodiesel"),
  attribute = rep(c("lhv", "ef_co2"), c(5, 4)),
  kind = rep(c("property", "factor"), c(5, 4)),
  value = c(28, 25, 10, 50, 37, 95000, 100000, 55000, 70000),
  unit_of_measure = rep(c("GJ/t", "kg/TJ"), c(5, 4)),
  source = "example"
)
codes <- data.frame(
  frame = c("carrier", "fuel", "carrier", "carrier"),
  member = c("Gas", "Lignite", "Electricity", "Coal"),
  alias = c("GAS", "LIG", "ELC", "coal"),
  source = "commodity"
)
fuels <- scale_from_leaftable(
  data.frame(
    group = c("Fossil", "Fossil", "Fossil", "Fossil", "Fossil", "Fossil",
              "Renewable", "Electricity"),
    carrier = c("Coal", "Coal", "Coal", "Gas", "Gas", "Oil", "Biofuel",
                "Electricity"),
    fuel = c("Anthracite", "Bituminous", "Lignite", "NaturalGas", "LNG",
             "Diesel", "Biodiesel", "Electricity")
  ),
  frames = c("group", "carrier", "fuel"), leaf = "fuel", name = "fuels",
  attributes = values, aliases = codes
)
fuels
#> NestedScale: fuels
#> Frames (3, coarsest first):
#>   - group (3)
#>     - carrier (5)
#>       - fuel (8)
#> Leaves: 8
#> Attributes: lhv, ef_co2 (sources: example) -- 9 at fuel
#> Aliases: 4 (commodity)
scale_members(fuels, "carrier")
#> [1] "Coal"        "Gas"         "Oil"         "Biofuel"     "Electricity"
scale_children(fuels, "carrier", "Coal")
#> [1] "Anthracite" "Bituminous" "Lignite"

Codes repeat across frames (Electricity is a group, the carrier inside it and that carrier’s only fuel), so every lookup names its frame.

Where a fuel has no value, there is no number – the package never fills one in:

lhv <- scale_attributes(fuels, "lhv", frame = "fuel")
lhv[c("member", "value", "unit_of_measure", "source")]
#>        member value unit_of_measure  source
#> 1  Anthracite    28            GJ/t example
#> 2  Bituminous    25            GJ/t example
#> 3     Lignite    10            GJ/t example
#> 4  NaturalGas    50            GJ/t example
#> 5         LNG    NA            <NA>    <NA>
#> 6      Diesel    NA            <NA>    <NA>
#> 7   Biodiesel    37            GJ/t example
#> 8 Electricity    NA            <NA>    <NA>

Attributes are not weights

A weight says how big a leaf is: hours in a time slice, area of a region, consumption of a fuel. Weights drive aggregation (weighted_mean up) and disaggregation (sum split down). They are declared on the leaftable and sum over the scale.

A calorific value is none of those things. It is a conversion factor: it turns a tonne of this fuel into gigajoules, row by row, and summing it over fuels is meaningless. So a scale keeps attributes in a separate table, keyed by (frame, member), and consumes them only in convert_scale(). The constructor promotes numeric leaftable columns to weights; a calorific value passed as a column would become a weight and be summed. Pass it as attributes=.

Averaging an attribute over a fuel mix is a legitimate aggregation – the mean calorific value of “coal” given how much of each coal is burnt. That is an ordinary recast of a resolved attribute with the weighted_mean rule, and the weight is where weights live: on the scale, as the consumption of each fuel.

coal <- filter_scale(fuels, "carrier", "Coal")
lt <- scale_leaftable(coal)
lt$tj <- c(100, 300, 400)
mix <- scale_from_leaftable(
  lt, frames = c("group", "carrier", "fuel"), leaf = "fuel",
  attributes = scale_attributes(coal), name = "mix"
)
lhv_coal <- scale_attributes(mix, "lhv", frame = "fuel")
recast_scale(
  data.frame(fuel = lhv_coal$member, lhv = lhv_coal$value), mix,
  source = "fuel", target = "carrier", rule = "weighted_mean", weight = "tj"
)
#>   carrier    lhv
#> 1    Coal 17.875

(filter_scale() keeps only the attribute rows of the surviving members, so the subset’s table is exactly what the new scale may take.)

Attributes live at any frame, and resolve by nearest ancestor

A value may be stored on a fuel, on a carrier or on a group. When a fuel has no value of its own, scale_attributes() walks to the nearest coarser frame that holds one and reports where the value came from. The example values are all at the fuel level; a carrier-level figure from another source fills the gaps below it without touching the fuels that have their own:

gas <- attach_attributes_scale(
  fuels,
  data.frame(frame = "carrier", member = "Gas", attribute = "lhv",
             kind = "property", value = 46, unit_of_measure = "GJ/t"),
  source = "carrier-level"
)
res <- scale_attributes(gas, "lhv", frame = "fuel")
res[res$member %in% scale_children(gas, "carrier", "Gas"),
    c("member", "value", "source", "origin_frame", "origin_member")]
#>       member value        source origin_frame origin_member
#> 4 NaturalGas    50       example         fuel    NaturalGas
#> 5        LNG    46 carrier-level      carrier           Gas

NaturalGas keeps its own value; LNG inherits the carrier’s. Nothing is guessed from a sibling or an average.

Two situations are refused rather than resolved:

  • Ambiguity across a cross-cutting frame. When the walk reaches a frame where the member has several ancestors and one of them holds the attribute, it cannot pick one and errors; if none does, it continues to the next coarser frame. vignette("anatomy") builds a scale with such a frame.
  • Several sources. Two sources publishing the same attribute for the same member is an error unless source= chooses. The walk stays within the chosen source: a source that lacks a fuel reports NA rather than borrowing another’s figure.
two <- attach_attributes_scale(
  fuels,
  data.frame(frame = "fuel", member = "Anthracite", attribute = "lhv",
             kind = "property", value = 27.5, unit_of_measure = "GJ/t"),
  source = "other"
)
scale_attributes(two, "lhv", frame = "fuel")
#> Error:
#> ! `lhv` for `Anthracite` at frame `fuel` is published by several sources (example, other); pass `source=`
other <- scale_attributes(two, "lhv", frame = "fuel", source = "other")
other[!is.na(other$value), c("member", "value", "source")]
#>       member value source
#> 1 Anthracite  27.5  other

Sources and provenance

Every attribute row names its source and unit_of_measure. Attaching never overwrites: a row with the same (frame, member, attribute, source) is an error, so the way to add a better number is to attach it under its own source name and select it. Every attribute name carries a kind (SCALE_ATTRIBUTE_KINDS): a property is an invertible ratio, a factor converts one way only. Any attribute name is accepted.

Mass to energy, with the calorific value

convert_scale() multiplies each row by the attribute resolved for its fuel. lhv is stored in GJ/t, so the direction is tonnes to gigajoules; the result reports which factor was applied and where it came from.

use <- data.frame(
  fuel = c("Anthracite", "Lignite", "NaturalGas", "Biodiesel"),
  kt   = c(120, 900, 0, 15)
)
use$t <- use$kt * 1e3                 # kt -> t: no prefix arithmetic is done
energy <- convert_scale(use[c("fuel", "t")], fuels, "lhv",
                        from_unit = "t", to_unit = "GJ")
energy
#>         fuel       t lhv lhv.origin_frame
#> 1 Anthracite 3360000  28             fuel
#> 2    Lignite 9000000  10             fuel
#> 3 NaturalGas       0  50             fuel
#> 4  Biodiesel  555000  37             fuel

A fuel without a value is an error, not a silent zero. Pass na_action = "keep" to carry NA instead. A property converts both ways:

convert_scale(energy[c("fuel", "t")], fuels, "lhv",
              from_unit = "GJ", to_unit = "t")
#>         fuel      t lhv lhv.origin_frame
#> 1 Anthracite 120000  28             fuel
#> 2    Lignite 900000  10             fuel
#> 3 NaturalGas      0  50             fuel
#> 4  Biodiesel  15000  37             fuel

Aggregate to carriers

Aggregation is a recast with an explicit rule; sum conserves the total. Register the rule once per column, or pass rule= each time.

One decision has to be stated. The table reports four fuels against a taxonomy of eight. By default an absent fuel is unknown, and every carrier that contains one aggregates to NA with a warning – the safe reading for incomplete data. Fuel statistics usually mean the other thing, that an unreported fuel was not used, and missing_sources = "ignore" says so.

tj <- data.frame(fuel = energy$fuel, tj = energy$t / 1e3)   # GJ -> TJ
register_scale_rule("tj", "sum")
by_carrier <- recast_scale(tj, fuels, source = "fuel", target = "carrier",
                           missing_sources = "ignore")
#> Warning: 4 source member(s) present in the scale but missing from the data
#> (e.g. Bituminous, Diesel, Electricity, ... (4 total)); produced NAs
by_carrier[which(by_carrier$tj > 0), ]
#>   carrier    tj
#> 1    Coal 12360
#> 4 Biofuel   555
sum(by_carrier$tj, na.rm = TRUE) == sum(tj$tj)
#> [1] TRUE

Emissions, one-way

An emission factor converts energy to CO2 and nothing else: convert_scale() refuses the inverse because ef_co2 is stored with kind factor, not property.

co2 <- convert_scale(tj, fuels, "ef_co2", from_unit = "TJ", to_unit = "kg")
names(co2)[names(co2) == "tj"] <- "co2_kg"
co2
#>         fuel    co2_kg ef_co2 ef_co2.origin_frame
#> 1 Anthracite 319200000  95000                fuel
#> 2    Lignite 900000000 100000                fuel
#> 3 NaturalGas         0  55000                fuel
#> 4  Biodiesel  38850000  70000                fuel
convert_scale(tj, fuels, "ef_co2", from_unit = "kg", to_unit = "TJ")
#> Error:
#> ! `ef_co2` converts TJ -> kg only; the inverse is refused because it is a factor, not a property (see SCALE_ATTRIBUTE_KINDS)

Values from a published source

Reference values – the defaults of an inventory guideline, the figures of a national statistical office, a plant-level measurement – are attached the same way: a table with one row per member and attribute, under the name of its source. Each source is chosen with source= when reading; nothing is overwritten.

mine <- attach_attributes_scale(
  fuels,
  data.frame(frame = "fuel", member = "Lignite", attribute = "lhv",
             kind = "property", value = 8.4, unit_of_measure = "GJ/t"),
  source = "plant"
)
plant <- scale_attributes(mine, "lhv", frame = "fuel", source = "plant")
plant[!is.na(plant$value), c("member", "value", "source")]
#>    member value source
#> 3 Lignite   8.4  plant

Model commodity codes

Models key fuels by short codes. scale_match() resolves them through the alias table, exactly and case-insensitively, first against member names and then against aliases, and reports ambiguity instead of guessing. There is no fuzzy or substring stage: a model input is not the place for a near miss.

scale_match(fuels, c("GAS", "LIG", "ELC", "Electricity"))
#>         label   frame      member    method
#> 1         GAS carrier         Gas     exact
#> 2         LIG    fuel     Lignite     alias
#> 3         ELC carrier Electricity     alias
#> 4 Electricity    <NA>        <NA> ambiguous
#>                                                 candidates
#> 1                                                     <NA>
#> 2                                                     <NA>
#> 3                                                     <NA>
#> 4 group/Electricity; carrier/Electricity; fuel/Electricity
scale_match(fuels, "Electricity", frame = "carrier")
#>         label   frame      member method candidates
#> 1 Electricity carrier Electricity  exact       <NA>

Attaching the hierarchy, and colours

A table keyed by fuel gets its carrier and group with one join; the added columns are prefixed by the scale’s name, so a second scale on the same table never collides with the first.

join_scale(use[c("fuel", "kt")], fuels, frame = "fuel", attach = TRUE)
#>         fuel  kt fuels.group fuels.carrier      fuels
#> 1 Anthracite 120      Fossil          Coal Anthracite
#> 2    Lignite 900      Fossil          Coal    Lignite
#> 3 NaturalGas   0      Fossil           Gas NaturalGas
#> 4  Biodiesel  15   Renewable       Biofuel  Biodiesel

Colours are presentation and are not stored on a scale. When a figure needs them, join them by member name from the palette it uses – the article Fuels, regions and months on the package site does so.

Country-specific values

Published defaults are usually global. A calorific value for hard coal in one country is the same attribute at the same fuel with a different region – a second dimension, not a deeper frame. That belongs to a scale_product() of the fuel scale and a GeoScale from geoscales, with the regional values attached as their own source; it is not built in this version.
